result.finding: Assessed 5 CWE rules in Credentials & Secrets: 1 FOUND, 4 NOT_FOUND
evidence: Inspected application C#/Razor/configuration and credential consumption paths with all values withheld. No hard-coded password, application cryptographic key or explicit unsafe ACL assignment confirmed.

NYCJobsWeb/Web.config:10 and DataLoader/DataLoader/App.config:5 contain placeholders, not verified live search keys. Browser map key reported separately with public-client/unknown-restrictions qualification.

Application has public read-only endpoints, not a local login/authentication implementation. Console logging exists in query/import catches, but deployment log capture is unknown; insufficient logging was not asserted solely from missing logging framework.

Static credential-pattern assessment only: no secret validity checks, network authentication attempts, tenant/IAM checks, ACL inspection, git-history secret scan or production logging validation. NOT_FOUND is not proof of secret absence.

values.name: Use of Hard-coded Password
values.description: The product contains a hard-coded password, which it uses for its own inbound authentication or for outbound communication to external components.

values.name: Use of Hard-coded Cryptographic Key
values.description: The product uses a hard-coded, unchangeable cryptographic key.

values.name: Incorrect Permission Assignment for Critical Resource
values.description: The product specifies permissions for a security-critical resource in a way that allows that resource to be read or modified by unintended actors.

values.name: Insufficient Logging
values.description: When a security-critical event occurs, the product either does not record the event or omits important details about the event when logging it.

values.name: Use of Hard-coded Credentials
values.description: The product contains hard-coded credentials, such as a password or cryptographic key.

evidence.explanation: Home view GetMap passes a non-placeholder, hard-coded Bing Maps credential to the browser map constructor at line 114. The credential is persisted in source and delivered to every page visitor. Value intentionally redacted and never tested. Browser map keys may be intentionally public; validity, domain/referrer restrictions, allowed APIs, billing exposure and administrative capability are unknown. This is a confirmed embedded API credential pattern, not evidence that a privileged server secret is active. Search service configuration values are placeholders or empty and are not reported as real credentials.
